s: Which university made the first global map of continental mantle earthquakes?
x: Stanford made the first global map of rare quakes that start more than 80 km below the Moho in the continental mantle.

s: Which country was hit by a seismic doublet of M 7.1 and M 7.5 in June 2026?
x: On 26 June 2026 a seismic doublet (M 7.1 and M 7.5) hit Caracas, Venezuela, on the Caribbean–South American strike-slip boundary.

s:
Consider the following statements about earthquakes:
1. An earthquake is a geological disaster, not an atmospheric one.
2. The time, place and magnitude of an earthquake can now be predicted accurately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Earthquakes are geological disasters and still cannot be predicted accurately in time, place and magnitude.

s: Which of the following is a geological disaster?
x: An earthquake comes from movements inside the Earth, so it is geological; the others are atmospheric.

s: In which year did the world's largest recorded earthquake, of magnitude 9.5, strike Chile?
x: The M 9.5 Chile earthquake of 22 May 1960 is the largest ever recorded.

s: Along which fault did the 2025 Myanmar (Mandalay) earthquake occur?
x: The 2025 Myanmar earthquake (M 7.7) was on the strike-slip Sagaing Fault between the Indian and Eurasian plates; Turkey-Syria 2023 was on the East Anatolian Fault.

s: The 1993 Latur earthquake was significant because it occurred in an intraplate region that had earlier been rated as which risk zone?
x: The Latur earthquake occurred in an intraplate region that was then classified as low-risk Zone I.

s: What was the magnitude of the 2015 Gorkha earthquake in Nepal, along the Main Himalayan Thrust?
x: The 2015 Gorkha earthquake had a magnitude of 7.8 and caused liquefaction in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.

s: Which earthquake, along with the 2004 tsunami, pushed India toward the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
x: The 2001 Bhuj earthquake was a turning point in disaster management and, with the 2004 tsunami, led to the DM Act, 2005.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Kangra earthquake struck in 1905. The Assam quake was in 1897, Bihar–Nepal in 1934 and Assam–Tibet in 1950.

s:
Assertion (A): The Koyna earthquake occurred in 1967 and involved reservoir-induced seismicity.
Reason (R): The Koyna earthquake had a magnitude of 6.3.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: the 1967 Koyna quake was reservoir-induced, and its magnitude was 6.3. Its magnitude does not explain its cause, so R does not explain A.

s: Why was the M 8.8 megathrust earthquake off Kamchatka in August 2025 notable?
o: Produced a tsunami that completely inundated the Pacific coast
Occurred on the Caracas strike-slip boundary
x: Despite its M 8.8 megathrust magnitude, the Kamchatka earthquake caused only a limited tsunami.

s: Along which fault did the February 2023 Turkey–Syria earthquake occur?
x: The Turkey–Syria earthquake of February 2023 occurred on the East Anatolian Fault.

s: The 2011 Tohoku earthquake of Japan resulted from the subduction of which plate?
x: Tohoku (M 9.0–9.1) was a Pacific plate subduction quake that caused a tsunami and the Fukushima disaster.

s: In which setting did the Uttarkashi earthquake of 20 October 1991 (Mw 6.8) occur?
x: The 1991 Uttarkashi earthquake was a Himalayan thrust zone event.

s: Which Indian earthquake of 1950, magnitude 8.6, is among the largest ever recorded?
x: The 1950 Assam–Tibet quake (8.6) is among the largest recorded; Kangra was 1905 and Bihar–Nepal 1934.

s: The April 2026 Koraput–Jeypore earthquake in Odisha was felt in which places of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The M 4.4 quake of 6 April 2026 shook Araku and Paderu in Alluri Sitharama Raju district.

s: In which year did the Bhuj (Kutch) earthquake of magnitude 7.7 occur?
x: The Bhuj earthquake struck Kutch on 26 January 2001 with magnitude 7.7, killing over 20,000 people.

s: What was the magnitude of the Bhuj earthquake of 26 January 2001?
x: The Bhuj (Kutch) earthquake of 26 January 2001 had a magnitude of 7.7.

s:
Arrange the following earthquakes of India in chronological order:
A. Latur
B. Koyna
C. Bhuj
D. Uttarkashi
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Koyna 1967, Uttarkashi 1991, Latur 1993 and Bhuj 2001.

s:
Match the following earthquakes of 2025-26 with their countries:
List-I
a. Kamchatka (Aug 2025)
b. Mindanao (Jun 2026)
c. Kyushu (Jul 2026)
d. Flores (Aug 2026)
List-II
I. Japan
II. Indonesia
III. Russia
IV. Philippines
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Kamchatka is in Russia, Mindanao in the Philippines, Kyushu in Japan and Flores in Indonesia.

s: The Sagaing Fault of Myanmar marks the boundary between which plates?
x: The Sagaing Fault is the Indian–Eurasian boundary where the Alpine-Himalayan belt continues into Myanmar.

s: Which combination of conditions is most conducive to the generation of a tsunami?
o: Magnitude below 5.0, deep focus and horizontal movement only
Magnitude above 6.5, shallow focus and vertical uplift of the sea floor
Volcanic ash fall without any displacement of water
Deep continental earthquake and subsidence of an inland basin
x: A tsunami generally requires an earthquake of magnitude greater than 6.5, a focus shallower than approximately 70 km and vertical uplift of the sea floor.

s: India developed its Tsunami Early Warning System after which event?
x: India built its Tsunami Early Warning System after the 2004 Sumatra earthquake and tsunami.

s: What are seismic seiches?
o: standing waves in rivers, reservoirs and ponds
waves generated only by volcanic ash
x: Seismic seiches are standing waves that may develop in enclosed or partly enclosed water bodies such as rivers, reservoirs and ponds. They were reported during the Myanmar earthquake.

s: Earthquake-induced liquefaction is a particular concern in which region of India?
x: Liquefaction is a particular concern in the alluvial Indo-Gangetic plain.

s: What mainly causes fires after an earthquake?
x: Fires result from broken gas and power lines; seiches occur in lakes and reservoirs.

s: In which type of buildings do about 95% of earthquake deaths occur?
o: Poorly built one- to three-storey houses
x: About 95% of earthquake deaths occur in poorly built one- to three-storey houses.

s: From which type of earthquakes do over 80% of tsunamis originate?
x: Over 80% of tsunamis come from megathrust subduction earthquakes, which lift the sea floor vertically.

s: Earthquake-triggered landslides are a major concern in which region of India?
x: Landslides are linked to the fragile Himalaya and North-East; the Indo-Gangetic Plain is prone to liquefaction instead.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Ring of Fire is associated mainly with volcanic and convergent-margin activity, not with the San Andreas-type transform setting. The San Andreas Fault is the transform-boundary example.

s: What are earthquakes that occur when stress on a fault exceeds rock strength and the rock ruptures called?
x: A tectonic earthquake is fault rupture when stress exceeds rock strength; it can occur at divergent as well as convergent boundaries.

s: What did the 1993 Latur earthquake demonstrate about the causes of earthquakes?
o: earthquakes may occur in stable regions along hidden faults
earthquakes occur only at convergent plate boundaries
all intraplate earthquakes are caused by volcanic eruptions
stable continental regions cannot experience damaging earthquakes
x: The Latur earthquake occurred far from a plate boundary and showed that stable continental regions can experience earthquakes along concealed or old faults.

s: Which one of the following is regarded as India's classic example of a reservoir-induced earthquake?
x: The Koyna earthquake of 1967 is the classic Indian example of reservoir-induced seismicity, associated with the filling and weight of a large reservoir.

s: Which of the following is NOT an induced cause of earthquakes?
o: Movement along the San Andreas Fault
x: San Andreas movement is tectonic; mining, hydraulic fracturing and reservoir filling induce earthquakes, usually of low magnitude.

s: The National Centre for Seismology detects which combination of earthquakes through its monitoring network?
o: Only earthquakes capable of producing tsunamis
Indian earthquakes of magnitude 3.0 and above and global earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 and above
Indian earthquakes of magnitude 1.0 and global earthquakes of magnitude 3.0 and above
Only earthquakes occurring in the Himalayan region
x: The National Centre for Seismology's National Seismological Network detects Indian earthquakes of magnitude 3.0 and above and global earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 and above.

s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: National Centre for Seismology – Real-time monitoring and earthquake information
NDMA – Policy guidelines and National Earthquake Risk Mitigation Project
BIS Code IS 1893 – Earthquake-resistant design of structures
x: NDRF does specialised search and rescue, including CSSR; earthquake-resistant design is covered by IS 1893.

s: The first seismological observatory in India was established at which place in 1898?
x: India’s first seismological observatory was established at Alipore in Calcutta in 1898.

s: RISEQ, the earthquake-related app of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is now known by which name?
x: The MoES app RISEQ is now called “Bhookamp.” IndiaQuake is the public-alert app of the National Centre for Seismology.

s: The National Seismological Network run by NCS has about how many observatories?
x: The NCS runs the National Seismological Network of about 160 observatories.

s: The National Centre for Seismology functions under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: NCS, based in New Delhi, is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).

s: For which cities have detailed seismic microzonation maps been prepared?
x: Microzonation gives detailed earthquake-risk maps; such maps have been made for Delhi and Guwahati.

s: Which force carries out specialised search and rescue, including collapsed structure search and rescue (CSSR), after earthquakes?
x: The National Disaster Response Force does specialised search and rescue, including CSSR.

s: What is the name of the public earthquake-alert app of the National Centre for Seismology?
x: IndiaQuake is the NCS app for earthquake alerts; Damini is for lightning and Meghdoot for farm weather.

s: Which institute developed 'Uttarakhand Bhookamp Alert', India's first earthquake early warning mobile app?
x: IIT Roorkee developed Uttarakhand Bhookamp Alert, launched in August 2021 as India's first earthquake early warning app.

s: Which State launched India's first earthquake early warning mobile app in 2021?
x: Uttarakhand launched the 'Uttarakhand Bhookamp Alert' app, developed by IIT Roorkee, on 4 August 2021.

s: What are the earthquakes associated with mid-oceanic ridges generally like?
x: Mid-oceanic ridge earthquakes are generally shallow and milder, reflecting activity at divergent plate boundaries.

s: Which one of the following belts is associated with the greatest concentration of earthquakes in the world?
x: The Circum-Pacific belt, also called the Ring of Fire, contains the world's greatest concentration of earthquakes and is associated largely with subduction around the Pacific basin.

s: With which plate setting is the Mediterranean-Himalayan seismic belt mainly associated?
o: A mantle plume beneath a moving plate
x: The Mediterranean-Himalayan belt is linked to continental collision; the Ring of Fire to subduction, the Mid-Atlantic belt to a divergent ridge and hotspots to mantle plumes.

s: About what share of the world's earthquakes occur in the Circum-Pacific belt?
x: The Circum-Pacific belt, a subduction setting, has about 90% of earthquakes; the 75% figure refers to active volcanoes.

s: The Pacific Ring of Fire holds about what share of the world's active volcanoes?
x: The Ring of Fire holds about 75% of active volcanoes, so it has the most eruptions.

s: With which of the following is volcanic activity in Hawaii and the Galapagos associated?
x: Hawaii and Galapagos lie over hotspots, where mantle plumes rise under a moving plate.

s: Japan, the most earthquake-prone nation of the world, lies on which seismic belt?
x: Japan lies on the Circum-Pacific (Ring of Fire) belt, which has about 90% of the world's earthquakes.

s: India forms part of which major seismic belt?
x: India lies in the Alpine-Himalayan seismic belt, which extends eastward through the North-East into Myanmar.

s: How are Love and Rayleigh waves collectively classified?
x: Love and Rayleigh waves move along the Earth's surface and are classified as surface waves.

s: What does the absence of S-waves beyond about 105° from the epicentre show about the Earth's outer core?
x: S-waves are transverse and travel through solids only, so their absence beyond about 105° shows the outer core is liquid.

s: Which seismic waves are the first to be recorded at a seismograph?
x: P (primary) waves are the fastest and arrive first; S-waves come second and surface waves last.

s: Which seismic waves can travel through solids only?
x: S-waves are transverse and pass through solids only, while P-waves travel through solids, liquids and gases.

s: What is the particle motion of P-waves?
o: Transverse, perpendicular to the direction of travel
Side to side along the surface
Longitudinal, push-pull along the direction of travel
x: P-waves are longitudinal push-pull waves; S-waves are transverse, Love waves side to side and Rayleigh waves rolling.

s: Which seismic waves arrive last and cause the most damage?
o: Both P and S waves equally
x: Surface waves are the slowest, arrive last and cause the most damage.

s:
Consider the following statements about seismic waves:
1. Love waves move the ground side to side.
2. Rayleigh waves have a rolling motion like ocean waves.
3. S-waves can pass through liquids.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. S-waves travel through solids only, which is why they do not cross the liquid outer core.
